title: Common Nodics Implementation Examples
readerIntent: Choose the correct Nodics ownership and extension pattern for common changes.
priorKnowledge: Read application capability, API, customization, testing, and documentation guides.
summary: Use these decision examples to place common changes in their existing authority instead of creating parallel implementations.

sections.heading: Examples
items: Add a field: extend the owning schema in a later project module, regenerate derived models/contracts, migrate or import data safely, and test old/new records.
Change a runtime value: expose it in properties.js and, only when operational updates are required, use the existing governed runtime configuration contract with validation, audit, and rollback.
Add an API: define an owned route, thin controller, facade orchestration, service behavior, schema model access, permissions, status codes, OpenAPI, and boundary tests.
Add a scheduled action: use CronJob with module/service identity; never reuse human username/password credentials.
Add a business approval: use Workflow actions that may be manual or automatic; do not turn a technical pipeline into a durable business process.
Integrate a provider: implement the existing provider-neutral adapter and selection configuration; callers must not reference the vendor directly.
Build a web UI: keep presentation/renderers in the client repository, load governed content and contracts, and call owning backend modules rather than placing business logic in the browser.

sections.heading: Review checklist
items: Existing authority searched and reused where possible.
Owner, contract, configuration, security, observability, failure/retry, performance, deployment, and rollback are explicit.
No duplicate loader, registry, persistence, workflow, API, or documentation authority exists.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, resilience, and regression evidence is present.
Canonical documentation and concise module README match the code.
